nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model estimated with HBR (PCNtoolkit) for DTI metrics across sites.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We extracted regional diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics using a standardized analysis and quality control protocol and used hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) to model the statistical distribution of derived WM metrics as a function of age and sex.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Normative models were built for fractional anisotropy (FA), and mean, radial, and axial diffusivity (MD/RD/AD) for 21 deep WM regions and the Global-WM.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We built normative models for the most widely used dMRI brain metrics - fractional anisotropy (FA), and mean, radial, and axial diffusivity (MD/RD/AD)

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age (modeled with cubic b-splines), sex, and dMRI scanning protocol (as batch effect) were used as explanatory variables.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We added age and sex as the covariates for the present study and we modeled the non-linear effect of age with a cubic b-spline basis set expansion... Consequently, we used the dMRI protocol as the batch effect when training the normative model with HBR.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Methods / 5. Normative Modeling with HBR & 6. Regression models
